title: Anchor toolchain bootstraps, introduce lightweight lint minifier, and stabilize dependency locks
author: Aisha Kapur
description:
Context and goal:
We observed repeated CI flakiness and long cold-start times caused by the ad-hoc collection of shell bootstraps for language toolchains (node/rust/go/python) and a heavy, monolithic lint runner that executes all rules for every PR. This PR introduces a two-part change: (1) a small, hermetic Go-based toolchain anchoring shim that canonicalizes bootstrapping steps and reduces runtime variability; (2) a lightweight lint 'minifier' runner used in fast-feedback lanes that runs a safe subset of rules and defers expensive or batch-only checks to nightly or staged lanes.

What changed (summary):
- Add tools/toolchain/anchor (Go) and migrate existing bootstrap snippets to canonical manifests. The shim consults a simple manifest (toolchain.yaml) and exposes a uniform local cache + lease mechanism for CI runners.
- Introduce tools/lint/minifier which implements a fast rule selector: rule tags, path-aware selectors, and a deterministic dry-run mode for presubmit.
- Add a lockfile anchoring step: ci/lock-anchors/anchor-check runs on PRs that change package manifests to ensure lockfile drift is deliberate. Anchoring tries to avoid full installs by validating lockfile checksums against curated anchors for transitive sets.
- Split CI workflow: .github/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml (uses minifier & anchor-check) and .github/workflows/presubmit-full.yml (daily/merge-only heavy runner).
- Migrate a set of existing bootstraps (ci/scripts/bootstrap-*.sh) to the new Go shim and remove duplicated logic.

Why this approach:
- Reduce presubmit latency by ~35-50% for common PRs via targeted linting and cache-friendly bootstraps.
- Reduce CI flakiness from environment drift by centralizing the bootstrap logic and blessable anchors.
- Make it easier to reason about which rules run in fast lanes and which run later (fewer noisy failures).

Checklist:
- [x] Add Go shim and minimal unit tests for manifest parsing
- [x] Implement minifier with path-aware rule selection and unit tests
- [x] Wire fast presubmit to minifier and anchor-check
- [x] Migrate 7 bootstrap scripts to toolchain anchor manifests
- [x] Update docs/ci/toolchain.md and docs/ci/lint-minifier.md
- [x] Run bench-scripts/presubmit-latency to validate improvement

Migration notes and rollback plan:
- New workflows default to opt-in on a subset of repos. Rollback involves re-enabling legacy bootstrap scripts (kept in tools/legacy-bootstraps) and reverting the workflow YAML. Anchor manifests are additive and safe to remove if rollback is required.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Anchor-check false positives when lockfile changes are legitimate (e.g., pinned transitive updates). Mitigation: anchor-check emits a clear remediation hint and a bypass label flow for trusted maintainers; it will not block merges by default until opt-in is complete.
- Risk: Minifier misses an important lint rule required for correctness. Mitigation: maintain a small required-rule tagset that always runs in fast lane; other rules are promoted via a staged rollout and telemetry.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on toolchain/anchor correctness and the deterministic nature of the lease cache. The Go shim is intentionally small; avoid bikeshedding the lease implementation unless correctness gaps are evident.

- Introduced toolchain anchor shim (tools/toolchain/anchor) to centralize bootstraps.
- Added lint minifier for fast-feedback lanes; heavy checks now run in presubmit-full/nightly.
